I’ve never voted for Donald Trump, but I’ve also never voted for any of his opponents in a general election. My voting history is complicated, kind of like my feelings — as a Never Trumper — about the Republican Party: I voted for Marco Rubio in the 2016 primaries, then sat out the general; crossed party lines in Virginia to vote for Joe Biden in the 2020 Democratic primaries (to stop Bernie Sanders), then wrote in Ronald Reagan for the general; and wrote in Reagan again in 2024.

A Brexit reversal is on the table 10 years on from the vote that changed Britain. Here’s what’s at stake

Britain voted to leave the European Union in 2016.

Actual Article Body:
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham suggested this week that British voters could be given the chance to reverse Brexit, the country's highly contentious departure from the European Union a decade ago.

Burnham, who became prime minister over the summer, told the BBC on Wednesday it was "possible" a referendum on rejoining the EU could be included in a future election manifesto.

A U.K. general election is not currently expected before 2029. Prime ministers are able to trigger an early snap election with the backing of parliament, but Burnham — who replaced predecessor Keir Starmer without a public vote — has ruled out such a move.

In his interview with the BBC, the prime minister said a referendum "wouldn't be the right thing to do right now," but added that the U.K. must "consider the options" for its relationship with the EU, arguing that "where we are isn't good enough."

Having a "Pre-COP" meeting in Fiji and Tuvalu is one of those initiatives that seemed a good idea at the time.

No doubt it still has resonance as part of Australia's wider diplomacy in the Pacific, in the battle to limit China's influence. But when Anthony Albanese, still coming down from his New York high, steps onto his plane on Monday bound for Pre-COP, it could feel more chore than opportunity.

Even COP itself, in Turkey a few weeks later and also on Albanese's itinerary, is not expected to break much ground.
